_comment: PreACT 10 Math blueprint (enhanced PreACT, aligned to the enhanced ACT): 36 multiple-choice questions, 45 minutes, four answer choices, the ACT's reporting categories, reported on the ACT's 1-36 scale with a top score of 35. Drawn from the ACT bank: the same items, minus the topics a tenth grader has not met (see _skillsByCategoryComment), on a lower difficulty curve. Scored through a raw-to-scale table equated to the ACT's (scaledScore), so a PreACT score reads as the ACT score that ability would earn, which is what the PreACT is for.
title: PreACT Math Practice Test
subject: preact-math
_categoryWeightsComment: The ACT's 9/8/8/9/6/5 scaled to 36 questions (x0.8) and rounded to sum to 36.
_authoredScaleComment: Until calibration measures an item (calibration.theta), its authored 1-5 difficulty orders the form. act-ies-expansion rated by position within each skill (a fixed 8/12/14/10/6 quota per skill), not by content, so its 4s and 5s include easy items that landed among the hardest questions. Its authored scale is mapped onto [min, max] for ordering only; calibrated items ignore this. Remove the entry once the bank is calibrated from real responses.
_difficultyRampComment: A band below the ACT's 1.5 -> 5.0: the PreACT is built for tenth graders, so the last questions are hard-for-a-sophomore rather than the ACT's hardest.
_skillsByCategoryComment: The ACT's skills minus the ones beyond a typical tenth grader: matrices and vectors, logarithms, the laws of sines and cosines, and trigonometric functions (right-triangle trig stays). Every category keeps at least three. Complex numbers are IN: ACT's PreACT guide puts real and complex number systems under Number & Quantity, and students who sat the real PreACT 10 (fall 2026) met powers of i (i^3) that this form never served. They were excluded at launch on a guess about tenth-grade scope; don't remove them again without the real test's word.
_excludePromptsComment: Items inside an in-scope skill whose TASK is beyond the PreACT 10: rational-function asymptotes (act-radical-rational-equations keeps its rational equations) and f(-x) reflections (act-graph-transformations keeps shifts, stretches and -f(x)). Two of four PreACT forms carried an asymptote item (QA pass, 2026-10-13). Case-insensitive regex sources matched against the prompt (utils/actTestAssembler.js excludedPrompts); the ACT blueprint draws them as before.

scaledScore._comment: Raw (0..36 on THIS form) -> estimated score on the ACT 1-36 scale, capped at 35 (the PreACT 10 top score). Equated through the ACT form: each raw score is the ability at which this 36-item ramp expects that many right, read off our ACT form's published raw-to-scale table (act-math-blueprint.json scaledScore) at the raw that ability earns there. So a PreACT score reads as the ACT score that ability would earn, which is what the PreACT is for. A blank sheet is 1, as on the ACT.
